title: English Practice Test 1 - English - Production of Writing
subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion.

 Using traditional Brazilian ingredients, such as manioc root and even ants—in innovative ways, he has **thrilled** diners from around the world.

The writer wants to emphasize the positive experience diners have had at Atala’s restaurant. Which choice best accomplishes that goal?
options: No Change
mystified
shocked
startled
questions.explain: 'Thrilled' is the only option that directly communicates a distinctly positive experience, which matches the writer's stated goal.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpts from consecutive paragraphs and consider the bolded portion.

 ...he has thrilled diners from around the world.
 
 **Still, Atala felt he could do more for his country and its cuisine.** In 2012, he founded Instituto Atá to help promote lesser-known ingredients...

Given that all the choices are accurate, which one provides the best transition from the preceding paragraph to this paragraph?
options: No Change
Atala is known for sometimes incorporating fragrances into his dishes as well.
In fact, Atala’s culinary training took place in classic European restaurants.
Atala’s obvious affection for his homeland is said to be infectious.
questions.explain: The original phrase transitions perfectly by acknowledging his existing success ('Still') while shifting the focus to his broader ambitions for his country, directly leading into his founding of Instituto Atá.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which transition word or phrase is most logical in context?

 This circumstance allowed her to retain her financial status without incurring responsibilities to a husband and children. **Nevertheless**, Hrosvitha had a greater level of independence—she could acquire property, receive guests, employ servants, and visit the royal court—than most women of her time.
options: No Change
On the other hand,
As a result,
In contrast,
questions.explain: The second sentence describes a direct outcome of the circumstance mentioned in the previous sentence. Thus, 'As a result,' provides the most logical cause-and-effect transition.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion.

 Hrosvitha produced at least eight narrative religious poems, two historical epics **(about the court of Otto I and Gandersheim)**, and six comedy-dramas.

Which choice best helps indicate that each historical epic covered different subject matter?
options: No Change
(each focused on the court of Otto I and
(focusing on the court of Otto I as well as
(one about the court of Otto I, the other about
questions.explain: Option d explicitly clarifies that there are two historical epics with distinct subjects ('one about..., the other about...').
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion.

 Normal rumble strips create that loud, grating noise when you drive over them—**like a built-in alarm for drivers who drift too close to the road’s edge.**

If the writer were to delete the bolded portion (adjusting the punctuation as needed), the paragraph would primarily lose:
options: information that indicates how prevalent rumble strips are on roadways.
a detail that reveals the narrator’s opinion of distracted drivers.
information that clarifies a primary function of rumble strips.
a detail that indicates what the rumble strips look like.
questions.explain: The bolded phrase ('like a built-in alarm for drivers who drift too close...') explicitly explains the primary safety purpose of traditional rumble strips. Deleting it would remove this functional clarification.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion.

 Even though constant traffic has worn down the musical rumble strips and warped the sound of some of the notes, **there are currently no plans to restore the strips.**
 
 After the last one of the notes fades into the darkening sky, I glance back at the boys, who have been lulled by the wonder of the song. I stop worrying about work...

Given that all the choices are accurate, which one most effectively leads into the rest of the essay?
options: No Change
lots of other drivers, not just me, still make this detour to hear the tune.
sometimes drivers will turn around and drive over the strips again.
this detour on our drive home never fails to buoy my spirits.
questions.explain: The sentence introducing the final paragraph talks about the narrator's emotional shift (stopping worrying about work, being relaxed by the boys' calmness). Option d sets up this positive psychological effect effectively.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which transition word or phrase is most logical in context?

 I stop worrying about work, about how many toy cars might have gotten lost between there and home. **Until then,** I feel like everything is going to be just fine.
options: No Change
Now and then,
For now,
Later,
questions.explain: 'For now' correctly reflects the narrator's temporary but genuine feeling of peace in the moment, making it a logical transition.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt.

 I stop worrying about work, about how many toy cars might have gotten lost between there and home. For now, I feel like everything is going to be just fine.

At this point in the paragraph, the writer is considering adding the following accurate sentence:
 *I hear there is another musical road in the US, somewhere in California.*

Should the writer make this addition?
options: Yes, because it makes clear that the narrator has plans to travel on other musical roads.
Yes, because it indicates that the musical road in New Mexico is not unique.
No, because it draws the focus away from the New Mexico musical road and its effect on the narrator.
No, because it fails to provide specific details about the construction of the musical road in California.
questions.explain: The paragraph is focused tightly on the narrator's personal feelings of calm resulting from the specific detour in New Mexico. Introducing a random fact about California distracts from the emotional and localized conclusion.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Question 25 asks about the preceding passage as a whole. Consider the following points in the essay where a new sentence could be inserted:

 Point A (in Paragraph 1): I check my speed. **[A]** Carefully, I steer toward the fog line...
 Point B (in Paragraph 2): ...we hear the distinct strain of the song "America the Beautiful." **[B]** The road is playing us a song.
 Point C (in Paragraph 3): **[C]** For me, this brief musical interlude is a charming curiosity...
 Point D (in Paragraph 4): After the last one of the notes fades into the darkening sky, I glance back at the boys, who have been lulled by the wonder of the song. **[D]** I stop worrying about work...

The writer wants to add the following sentence to the essay:
 *It is marvelously quiet.*

The sentence would most logically be placed at:
options: Point A in Paragraph 1.
Point B in Paragraph 2.
Point C in Paragraph 3.
Point D in Paragraph 4.
questions.explain: At Point D, the passage notes that the song has faded and the squalling boys have been lulled. Adding 'It is marvelously quiet' precisely captures the auditory shift that has just taken place before the narrator's introspective conclusion.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion.

 ...provide stewardship (**legal and ethical management, care, documentation, and use**) of their collections. 

If the writer were to delete the bolded portion (adjusting the punctuation as needed), the essay would primarily lose a:
options: suggestion that not all public museums provide proper stewardship for their artifacts.
clarification of what public museum stewardship entails.
list of reasons for educating the public on stewardship.
description of the daily tasks performed by curators.
questions.explain: The parenthetical phrase defines and clarifies what "stewardship" means in the specific context of museum collections. Deleting it would remove this crucial clarification.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which transition word is most logical in context? 

 In a traditional museum display, each artifact is labeled and positioned at eye level with plenty of space between it and the other objects. **Subsequently,** artifacts in visible storage spaces are placed close together and are often displayed from floor to ceiling with few labels.
options: No Change
Conversely,
Namely,
Granted,
questions.explain: The second sentence describes a method of displaying items (placed close together, few labels) that strongly contrasts with the traditional museum display described in the first sentence (plenty of space, labeled). "Conversely" is the correct transition for highlighting a contrast.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt.

 While some artifacts can never be displayed, many pieces that can—and should—be viewed are not.

At this point, the writer is considering adding the following parenthetical phrase immediately after the word "displayed":
 *(whether because of light sensitivity or the request of a donor)*

Given that the information is accurate, should the writer make this addition here?
options: Yes, because it gives specific examples to help explain why some objects can never be displayed in a museum.
Yes, because it offers specific examples of items that require special storage.
No, because it detracts from the paragraph’s focus on the ideal museum layout.
No, because it diminishes the role museums play in educating the public.
questions.explain: The added text serves a clear functional purpose by illustrating explicitly *why* some items might never be able to be displayed, supporting the claim effectively.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Consider the following points where sentences might be added:

 ...acquiring additional items makes finding enough suitable storage space difficult, especially for delicate items. **[A]**
 
 To remain true to the goals of education and stewardship, museums should dedicate public access space to visible storage. **[B]** Also known as open storage, visible storage provides ways to display many items in small or irregular spaces, allowing more artifacts to be on exhibit. **[C]**
 
 In a traditional museum display... **[D]** 

The writer wants to add the following sentence to the essay:
 *This potentially compromises stewardship.*

For the sake of logic and cohesion, the sentence should be placed at:
options: Point A in Paragraph 1.
Point B in Paragraph 2.
Point C in Paragraph 2.
Point D in Paragraph 3.
questions.explain: Paragraph 1 discusses the negative impact of running out of suitable storage space for delicate artifacts. Placing the statement at Point A correctly connects these poor storage conditions with their overarching consequence: compromising stewardship.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion.

 Slung across the branches, each nest—**which can measure up to thirteen feet wide and seven feet thick**—is a sprawling community home to hundreds of birds.

If the writer were to delete the bolded phrase (adjusting the punctuation as needed), the sentence would primarily lose:
options: specific information that illustrates the minimum height at which the weavers begin building their nests.
specific information that underscores the enormousness of the weavers’ nests.
details that clarify how the weavers are able to survive in the Kalahari Desert.
details that explain how the weavers’ nests differ from other birds’ nests.
questions.explain: The phrase gives exact, large dimensions (thirteen feet wide and seven feet thick) directly confirming the claim that the nests are "enormous".
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion.

 Although the weavers use typical materials such as sticks, grass, and feathers to construct their nests, the nests look more like **disorganized piles**.

The writer wants to emphasize the unusual appearance of the weavers’ nests by using playful language to evoke a specific image. Which choice best accomplishes this goal?
options: No Change
carelessly plunked-down haystacks.
collections of disparate items.
large knots.
questions.explain: "Carelessly plunked-down haystacks" is the only option that utilizes vivid and playful language to establish a highly specific, unusual visual image.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt.

 **Paj ntaub is increasingly made in lighter, softer shades today.** She’s been creating stitched textiles since she was a young woman living in northern Laos. For the past several decades, she’s been designing paj ntaub in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, where she also teaches her craft.

The writer is considering deleting the bolded sentence. Should the sentence be kept or deleted?
options: Kept, because it compares Pang Xiong’s embroidery style with that of modern paj ntaub.
Kept, because it places the subject of the essay in a modern context.
Deleted, because it detracts from the paragraph’s focus on the various styles of ancient Hmong needlework arts.
Deleted, because it adds a detail that is irrelevant to the paragraph’s introduction of Pang Xiong’s connection to paj ntaub.
questions.explain: The paragraph introduces Pang Xiong's personal biographical background and lifetime practice of creating the needlework. Injecting a random fact about modern lighter shades is completely disconnected from this narrative thread.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion.

 Flower cloth **(commonly as a shirt, dress, coat, or collar)** is made to be worn as clothing and, depending on the amount of needlework on the piece, is designed either for everyday wear or for a special occasion.

The best placement for the bolded portion would be:
options: where it is now.
after the word made.
after the word clothing.
after the word needlework.
questions.explain: The parenthetical phrase lists examples of clothing items (shirt, dress, coat, etc.), meaning it logically and syntactically belongs immediately following the word "clothing" to clarify what that clothing looks like.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion.

 With pattern names such as “elephant’s foot” and “snail house” and images of animals framed by geometric designs, **paj ntaub patterns are versatile**.

Which choice most clearly builds on the information provided earlier in the sentence about a common theme in paj ntaub patterns and images?
options: No Change
only a master artist is able to create paj ntaub clothing for special occasions.
paj ntaub patterns are extraordinarily colorful.
paj ntaub celebrates the natural world.
questions.explain: The sentence specifically lists "elephant", "snail", and other "animals". Replacing "are versatile" with "celebrates the natural world" perfectly sums up this cohesive theme.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt.

 Pang Xiong regrets that most people she knows today wear only **regular** clothes. When she was growing up in Laos, she explains, she had few items of clothing, but each garment she owned was handcrafted paj ntaub.

The writer is considering revising the bolded portion to the following:
 *mass-produced*

Should the writer make this revision?
options: Yes, because the revision creates a clearer contrast between the homogeneous styles of clothing that are popular today and the handcrafted paj ntaub.
Yes, because the revision emphasizes Pang Xiong’s desire for her handcrafted paj ntaub to be sold on a large scale in stores.
No, because the original word reinforces the idea that although paj ntaub clothing can be used for everyday wear, it should be saved for special occasions.
No, because the original word more specifically describes the type of clothing Pang Xiong disapproves of.
questions.explain: Replacing "regular" with "mass-produced" establishes an exact antithesis to the word "handcrafted" appearing in the following sentence, strengthening the contrast.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the bolded portion. Which transition word or phrase, if any, is most logical in context? 

 When she was growing up in Laos, she explains, she had few items of clothing, but each garment she owned was handcrafted paj ntaub.
 
 **However, she** still wears flower cloth every day and would like to inspire others to do so.
options: No Change
For example, she
Besides, she
She
questions.explain: Because she used to wear handcrafted garments as a youth and *still* wears them today, a contrast word like "However" creates a logical error. Deleting it to simply say "She still wears..." permits the word "still" to accurately govern the transition.
questions.subject: English

questions.q:
Read the following excerpt and consider the placement of a new sentence at the end.

 Pang Xiong teaches paj ntaub in art museums—including at the Smithsonian Institution, where some of her textiles are on permanent display—and in community settings around Philadelphia. **[50]** Pang Xiong is showing a new generation the joys of paj ntaub and beautiful handcrafted clothing.

Which of the following true statements, if added at point [50], would best build on the ideas presented in this paragraph and connect to the final sentence of the essay?
options: She loves when people, no matter what their ethnicity, wear traditional clothing every day.
She often teaches paj ntaub to Hmong adults her age who want to learn new techniques.
Recently, she worked with nine young Hmong women in a formal apprenticeship.
One of her own favorite pieces tells the story of her family.
questions.explain: The final sentence specifically references showing a "new generation" her joys. The statement mentioning "young Hmong women" provides the perfect factual bridge to link her teaching endeavors directly to a "new generation."
questions.subject: English
